newsitem.title: UK: Tesco shares gain as results please.
newsitem.headline: Tesco shares gain as results please.

text.p: Shares in Tesco Plc rose to a two-month high on Tuesday as the market welcomed the supermarket group's results showing a 10.1 percent rise in pre-tax profit in the year through February.
With Tesco's figures bang in line with expectations, some dealers and analysts said they provided little fresh incentive for the stock -- yet others remained keen on Tesco's prospects.

Analysts at SBC Warburg retained an "add" rating on Tesco and said it remained a core holding in the sector. Tesco shares were up 6-1/2p at 359 by 0907 GMT in volume of 2.8 million shares, after touching 360p -- its highest since February 7.
One market-maker pointed to Tesco's statement showing a six percent rise in same-store sales in the first few weeks of the year as giving a boost to the stock.
However, others remained cool on Tesco and the sector as a whole, which has underperformed in recent months because of intense competition in the industry.
Supermarket stocks suffered a sharp fall on February 7 after Safeway Plc warned that profits could be hit by a slowdown in sales growth in the first 16 weeks of the second half.
"We didn't really see anything in the results of any great surprise but someone obviously likes them," said one dealer.
Tesco said pre-tax profit rose 10.1 percent to 750 million stg, in line with analyst expectations which ranged from 681 million stg to 760 million, according to the Estimate Directory.
The dividend was raised 7.8 percent to 10.35p, also in line with expectations.
UK same-store sales rose 7.5 percent though the petrol price war cut UK profit growth by some five percent and lowered overall operating margins by about 0.3 percent.

Tesco said sales had continued to move ahead in the early weeks of the current year, with same store sales up 6.0 percent from the year before, though price inflation had dropped to 1.0 percent from 3.5 percent in the second half of last year.
The company, which higlighted recent successful marketing initiatives such as its Clubcard scheme, said it was a "good start in a competitive environment."
